citation: Vasilev v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2026 FC 716
what_court_addressed: Whether misrepresentation automatically places fairness at the highest end and whether the concern was disclosed clearly enough
scoped_proposition: The duty of fairness in misrepresentation cases is heightened but remains contextual under Baker; not every misrepresentation case is automatically situated at the high end. Where the decision maker has identified a specific concern, a PFL stating only a general fraud concern may be insufficient if it does not disclose the specific concern with enough clarity to permit a meaningful response.
scope_comparator_control: Vasilev does not hold that every investigative detail must be disclosed in every case. Read alongside Ekpe 2026 FC 727, where a PFL identifying a bank document as likely fraudulent was sufficient on that record and the officer was not required to disclose the precise issue that prompted the bank inquiry.

citation: Ekpe v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2026 FC 727
what_court_addressed: Whether a PFL identifying a bank statement as likely fraudulent disclosed enough of the case to meet
scoped_proposition: Grammond J held that the process was fair on the record before the Court. A PFL stating that a bank document was likely fraudulent was sufficient to disclose the gist of the concern, and the officer was not required to disclose the precise issue that prompted the inquiry to the bank.
scope_comparator_control: Direct comparator to Vasilev, not later treatment of it. The two decisions were issued on consecutive days and Ekpe does not cite Vasilev. PFL adequacy remains fact- and context-specific.

citation: Agyemang v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2026 FC 30
program_issue_context: Study permit / misrepresentation / disclosure of actual concerns and extrinsic evidence
what_court_addressed: Whether the applicant received the officer's actual concerns and the material giving rise to them
scoped_proposition: Battista J held that, in the misrepresentation determination before the Court, procedural fairness required disclosure of the officer's actual concerns reflected in the file notes and disclosure of extrinsic evidence giving rise to those concerns, subject to justified limits such as privilege, national security, or circumstances warranting a summary.
scope_comparator_control: Read together with Vasilev 2026 FC 716. Do not state that every misrepresentation case always requires full disclosure or automatically sits at the high end of the fairness spectrum. Vasilev later adopted a materially different contextual Baker analysis.

citation: Odobo v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2026 FC 49
program_issue_context: LMIA-based work permit / misrepresentation / adequacy of PFL
what_court_addressed: Gap between generic PFL wording and materially more detailed concerns in GCMS notes
scoped_proposition: Applying Agyemang, Battista J found procedural unfairness where the PFL conveyed only a generic, minimal concern even though the GCMS notes recorded materially more detailed misrepresentation concerns; on those facts, the applicant was not given meaningful disclosure of the case to meet.
scope_comparator_control: Read together with Vasilev. Do not present Odobo as establishing an uncontested universal disclosure standard. The underlying positive-LMIA/job-offer genuineness issue also engaged R203(1)(a) and R200(5), but the proposition stated here is limited to procedural fairness.

citation: Ju v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2026 FC 236
program_issue_context: Saskatchewan nominee PR/work permit / employer documents / misrepresentation
what_court_addressed: New determinative employer concerns arising from documents apparently unavailable to the applicant
scoped_proposition: Where employer documents obtained after an interview generated determinative new concerns about the employer's commercial and human-resource circumstances, and the applicant did not appear to have access to those documents, procedural fairness was breached when the officers relied on those concerns without communicating them and giving the applicant a meaningful opportunity to respond.
scope_comparator_control: The Court did not decide the Applicant's reasonableness arguments; it expressly stated that its silence should not be perceived as endorsing the reasonableness of the decisions.

citation: Chater v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2026 FC 588
what_court_addressed: Whether the officer adequately explained materiality of omitted prior refusals
scoped_proposition: Materiality under A40(1)(a) cannot simply be presumed. On the record before the Court, a bare conclusion that an omission could have induced an error in the administration of IRPA was insufficient where the officer did not explain how the omitted prior visa refusals met the materiality requirement.
scope_comparator_control: The Court did not decide the separately argued innocent-mistake issue. This row concerns justification/materiality, not a procedural-fairness breach. Read with Righetti 2026 FC 830, where concise materiality reasons were upheld because the officer actually connected the prior refusals to the applicant's immigration history and a full assessment of eligibility/admissibility.

citation: Righetti v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2026 FC 830
program_issue_context: eTA / omitted prior work-permit refusals / fairness and materiality
what_court_addressed: Whether a further PFL or interview was required after the applicant responded, and whether the materiality reasons were sufficient
scoped_proposition: On the record before the Court, the PFL identified the statutory concern, the relevant application question and the factual basis involving three prior work-permit refusals. Because the applicant's response put his knowledge and the plausibility of his explanation squarely in issue without creating a new concern, no further PFL or interview was required merely because the officer rejected the explanation. The Court also upheld the officer's concise materiality analysis because the reasons explained why the prior refusals mattered to a full assessment of the applicant's immigration history, eligibility and admissibility.
scope_comparator_control: Comparator to Chater on omitted-refusal materiality, not later treatment of it. Righetti does not hold that materiality may be presumed or that reasons are unnecessary; it upheld concise reasons that actually articulated why the omitted information mattered.
